items.title: Disassembling qLDPC codes for depth-optimal parity-check circuits
items.authors: Minh T. P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Stefano Bosco
items.matched: High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory
items.headline: Disassembling qLDPC codes yields provably optimal or near-optimal CNOT depth for syndrome extraction circuits.
items.so_what: This approach enables more efficient and practical implementation of qLDPC codes for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
items.caveat: The depth-optimal circuits for Quantum Tanner codes were demonstrated on every instance tested, including codes up to nearly 600 data qubits.

items.title: Architecture and Compilation Co-Design for High-Rate Quantum Product Codes on Neutral Atom Arrays
items.authors: Adrian Liu, Wan-Hsuan Lin, Daniel Bochen Tan, Qian Xu, Jason Cong
items.matched: High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory
items.headline: The ONEX framework achieves 3.7x to 6.1x and 29.8x to 42.1x higher clock rates for hypergraph product (HGP) code memory compared to constructive 1D and general 2D compilers, respectively.
items.so_what: This framework provides provably depth-optimal physical execution plans for quantum product codes, significantly improving the efficiency and scalability of quantum error correction on neutral atom arrays.
items.caveat: The evaluation is performed for hypergraph product (HGP) code memory mapped onto neutral atom arrays, scaling to codes with 2,500 data qubits, and extended to the lifted-product (LP) code family.

items.title: Rethinking Quantum Circuits
items.authors: Steven Rayan
items.matched: Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
items.headline: This work develops four interconnected ways of reading a quantum circuit, from operational composition to geometric properties.
items.so_what: This framework offers a unified perspective on quantum circuits, integrating operational, diagrammatic, error-corrected, and geometric aspects.
items.caveat: The geometric interpretation relies on the prospect of physical superconducting circuits emulating negatively-curved lattices.

items.title: Logarithmic depth compression of Heisenberg Hamiltonian simulation by fan-out parallelization, with built-in error detection
items.authors: Artemiy Burov, Cl\'ement Javerzac
items.matched: High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory
items.headline: A fan-out-based gadget compiler reduces two-qubit circuit depth by up to 2.5-fold for Heisenberg-type NMR Hamiltonian simulations.
items.so_what: This method offers a way to significantly reduce circuit depth for simulating Heisenberg-type NMR Hamiltonians, potentially enabling more complex simulations on depth-limited quantum hardware, especially with improved error rates.
items.caveat: The method's benefits are realized only after post-selection on built-in error detection, once error rates improve by one to one and a half orders of magnitude.

items.title: Large Scale Entanglement Structure Detection in 100-Qubit Systems via Local Joint Measurements
items.authors: Rui Li, Yuhang Wang, Chunxiao Du, Shikun Zhang, Zheng Qin, Wenxiu Li, Hao Zhang, Zhisong Xiao
items.matched: Quantum error correction for quantum memories
items.headline: A new framework detects large-scale entanglement structures in 100-qubit systems with a mean accuracy exceeding 95% in noisy simulations.
items.so_what: This framework offers a scalable alternative to conventional tomography for identifying entanglement structures, overcoming exponential scaling with system size.
items.caveat: Hardware validation is limited to 13 qubits before noise- and depth-induced degradation sets in at larger sizes.

items.title: Phase information beyond entanglement sudden death in coherence-to-entanglement conversion under post-gate noise
items.authors: Asad Ali, Hashir Kuniyil, M. T Rahim, Saif Al-kuwari
items.matched: Universal quantum computation with ideal Clifford gates and noisy ancillas
items.headline:
Phase quantum Fisher information (QFI) can remain positive even when entanglement vanishes, with a residual QFI of $F_φ^
\star=1/6$ at maximal input coherence for global and independent local depolarization channels.
items.so_what: This means phase information can still be extracted from quantum states even after they become separable due to post-gate noise.
items.caveat: The results are reference benchmarks for phase-information retention, not a claim of metrological advantage.

items.title: The HALO Engine: $\mathcal{O}(1)$-Step Compilation and Localized String Rupture for Lattice Gauge Theories on Quantum Hardware
items.authors: Abhiroop Gohar
items.matched: Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit
items.headline: The HALO compiler identifies a topological transition at $t \approx 0.790$ lattice units with an $18.3 \pm 2.2\%$ rupture probability in a mesoscopic lattice.
items.so_what: This enables digital simulation of lattice gauge theories on near-term quantum hardware with constant circuit depth per Trotter step, overcoming a key limitation of standard Trotterization schemes.
items.caveat: The results were obtained for the Quantum Link Model truncation of the Schwinger model on a 16-qubit superconducting transmon processor.

items.title: The ebbs and flows of quantum learning and sensing
items.authors: Matias Karjula, Teemu Ojanen, Tapio Ala-Nissila, Moein N. Ivaki
items.matched: Barren plateaus in quantum neural network training landscapes
items.headline: An intermediate "learning phase" precedes quantum chaos, characterized by pronounced nonflatness and sensitivity of readout states, directly controlling ensemble-typical information processing power.
items.so_what: This suggests that features of random quantum dynamics can be leveraged as computational resources for scalable nonlinear computation.
items.caveat: The results are obtained by studying a family of minimally tunable postvariational quantum circuits.

items.title: Shadow models of a quantum model for cloud cover and the influence of finite sampling noise
items.authors: Hedwig Keller, Mierk Schwabe, Veronika Eyring
items.matched: Power of data in quantum machine learning
items.headline: Shadow models mitigate finite sampling noise and enable efficient classical reconstruction of quantum machine learning circuits for cloud cover.
items.so_what: Efficient coupling of quantum machine learning models to classical applications and mitigation of finite sampling noise become possible through shadow models.
items.caveat: under certain conditions, and error mitigating effects on quantum hardware are difficult to distinguish from calibration errors.

items.title: Parallel Quantum Advantage with Limited Adaptivity Requires Structure
items.authors: Qipeng Liu, Saachi Mutreja
items.matched: Power of data in quantum machine learning
items.headline: The Aaronson and Ambainis conjecture is proven for quantum algorithms that make massively parallel quantum queries.
items.so_what: This suggests that exponential quantum speedups are limited to sufficiently structured inputs under conditions of massively parallel or limited adaptive quantum queries.
items.caveat: The result applies to algorithms with massively parallel quantum queries or constant rounds of adaptivity.
